super chill. extended my exams when i asked him to. super nice dude. take him. he's great

its like a dream come true

Loved Prof Lisha's class! Very clear grading requirements/rubric. She also offers a late pass in case you don't have enough time to do an assignment up to week 10. Would recommend.

Was a really sweet professor that really engaged with the class and made me feel much more confident about my writing. The essays and assignments we had were also kind of fun so I would highly recommend!

This was one of the easiest classes I took at De Anza. If you complete the assignments before the due date, you can easily get an A.

Prof Kondo was nice. Gives EC points for answering/participating in lectures. Better hope you get good partners as you're working on a group project the entire quarter. Professor Kondo is a thoughtful and dedicated instructor who genuinely cares about his students' success. When the gates opened, he stepped forth, and that's when I saw his face. Standing in front of me, in all his godly grandiosity, was Nate Tan. I was frozen with awe. Professor Tan's real-world experience and deep compassion make his classes more than just lectures. He connects history to lived experiences and truly cares about his students. Wherever you are in your journey, he'll meet you there and help you grow.

Professor Tan's class was a breath of fresh air. His teaching invites introspection and connection to the world around us. He's deeply committed to his students and community, grounding lessons in lived experience and social context. Highly recommend if you want meaningful, thoughtful learning.

Professor Tan's knowledge, expertise and exhaustive experience working in the community make his lectures more than just book work. I got new inspirations and always want to play more. I was thinking about taking his class every semester, but he doesn't seem to teach lots of classes now, which is a pity.

MUSI 12B. Learned how to sight read and improvise with different chord styles, two assignments of scale fingerings, a midterm performance and final performance. You can choose songs from the textbook or bring your own songs to play. After each performance there is positive feedback only. Super talented and kind to everyone which leads to an easy A.
He's very patient and have lots of knowledge about jazz.

I'd think this class is a hidden gem in De Anza college. Really high quality self-printed (i.e. free) course material, well structured syllabus and clear instruction. Mr. Schneider also tons of fun and we often had a good laugh when the whole class did some improvisation experiment together.
The best jazz piano teacher ever! His instruction is very clear, helpful all the students in any level. His materials are very useful,interesting and inspring. I highly recommend the teacher!

she is kind, Follow the the instructions and rubric and you will pass. Her essay topics were difficult for me and get ready to read. there is so much reading in her class. She answers to messages fast.

I took the asynchronous version and to me it honestly was not that bad at all. All assignments were pretty easy, essays and research paper just take a lot longer. She gives a fair amount of extra credit and is pretty quick to respond to emails. As a grader, in my opinion she was not very difficult, just tailor your paper to the rubric and your good
She is kind and wants you to succeed. Follow the rubric for the essays and you will pass with an A. She also provides extra credit and responds to emails outside of school hours.

Modirzadeh's syllabus is clear and she follows it. Get ready to read, but the course content is interesting and thought provoking.  She meets with you as many times as you need to go over your writing. She holds regular office hours, so take advantage of that. Responds promptly to emails. She is a tough grader but gives good feedback.
Not very engaging during discussions. She tends to talk more about her opinions. Take someone else.

Professor Fox is a hilarious professor! He does give a lot of readings, but it pays off. I do think some students, such as international students might find one component of the class a bit difficult, as it did involve doing community service, which not everyone in the class might know the people to contact or resources to use

I'm a HS Senior who was not prepared for the workload of this course, especially in summer term. But it's one of the best classes I've ever taken. Professor John is such an empathetic prof--I missed a deadline due to a time zone difference and he completely understood and let me turn in the work late. If you're ready for the work, take this course!

Amazing prof. One of the few where the work is worth it. This class is paper heavy with textbook reading and response papers but it IS college level work. Lectures are packed with info and always interesting, thanks to his teaching style. Great attitude, funny, but don't be rude in his class, he'll call you out. Great material and prof. TAKE!

I liked John's class ! He has a unique way of teaching and he definitely has the knowledge on the subjects he is teaching on. EASY A, but you still learn interesting information. DEFINITELY TAKE HIM!!

One of my favorite teachers at De Anza. He respects his students and is very clear and concise in lecture. He engages his students well and encourages discussion. You can have fun in his classes, you just have to be expecting to write and read quite a bit. But what else is to be expected in college?

The amount of material need to study for each exam is immeasurable, she keep emphasize types of diseases for students to understand which many of the students cannot comprehend. Very difficult exams because half of the study material slides she does not share to students. MLT dept. should do course evaluation to voice out the concern from students

Hematology is very dense, and the pace of this class is very fast. However, the instructor is kind, approachable, and provides you with the resources to follow the lecture. She emphasizes understanding the material, rather than memorizing. You will have to work hard in this class

Lectures all over the place, reads the endless material on slides. Nightmare exams for MLT/CLS level. Pathophysiological based exams with long summary of patient's clinical history with RBC #, Platelets # , etc... then you have to find what disease the patient has. Professor knows that most students taking this class are not pre-medical students.

The lectures will benefit from better slide structure and better lecturer... They actual lectures are hard to understand for lack of consistency in her talking points, a lot of repetition and it is hard to catch up. She often stumble on her own note and cannot remember what she had to say...

She won't give anyone a letter of recommendation. She refuses to give her powerpoint pictures to you (you will get an outline). She goes over a lot of the pathophysiology, this class focus on diagnosing the patient. Exams are all online and only go forward! Meaning you can not go back to a question you already answered.
Tough class with picky grading. Use Unstuck ai and study groups to navigate expectations. Textbook is useful, but attend class for clarification.

Originally I was so excited to take this class.  However, it ended up being my worst experience with a teacher.  Unclear expectations, confusion over her grading, abrupt with her communications, and her use of canvas was frustrating.  Without my discord group I would have lost my mind.  I was so disappointed by her.  Do not take this class.
I got an A+ from her during the summer. She gave a lot of extra credit option but no video recording nor lecture. Just book reading. Not a good class take.

Was a very frustrating time during this class. Professor expects you to follow EVERY little detail she wants, will grade down an assignment for grammar or even providing too much detail or too little. Final was just awful, and you were expected to get a PERFECT grade in order to pass the class.

Grading and expectations are confusing. Weekly hw is talking to someone different ethnicity from you, convo need to pertain to chapter and video of that week. VERY unreasonable, especially those with work, or kids. Times to submit are specific (8PM TH/S) and won't accept anything a minute late. Annoyed as all other teachers are 11:59PM SUN

I wouldn't recommend this class if you heavily rely on good professors but in my experience I mostly self-studied and re-reviewed his recorded lectures in order to study for exams. I would say the difficulty is 7.75/10 but if you lack self discipline I would not take his class. I also don't like how he grades everything near the end of the quarter.

This professor is one of those professors that really want you to succeed. He is approachable and always willing to help during office hours or via email, making sure students understand the content.The high frequency of assessments requires a significant amount of study time and preparation. This is standard for most classes so I didn't mind.

Lacked communication, did not respond to any emails, and left students to email the dean of the department to figure out what was going on. He seems nice, but he did not do a good job with this quarter in particular. Sometimes he uploaded quizzes the day before it was due. Grade depends on quizzes/tests, you get 2-3 attempts on some quizzes.

Really nice professor, very flexible with exam times and hes always willing to try to help. Doesnt stay on topic and goes on rants for things we dont need to know. Exams are completely different from quizes so its hard to understand what we need to know. things that are important, he doesnt test, things that are very small and forgettable, he tests

His class is a struggle. He rarely stays on topic, often going off on long rants that have nothing to do with the class. He REALLY struggles with technology, which eats up chunks of class time, meaning you often don't even get to finish covering the topics you were supposed to that day. I haven't learned anything in his class so far. Not one.

Quite honestly one of the best professors I've had in a really long time, I took intro to anthro and her lab together. While I don't think the coursework matched with one another she always took time to make sure everyone had a clear understanding of the material. Attendance is usually taken through group discussions.

Average online summer class, pretty easy if you know what you're doing, cheesed my way through the class without buying the lab textbook (use demo version), lots of quizzes which are fairly easy/average, seems very caring through her replies, multiple attempts on all of her assignments besides exams, no extra credit, pretty decent choice overall

She is fine. She assigns way too many lecture videos and large reading documents. The 3 quizzes are more like huge exams that are both multiple choice and free response. You basically have to know everything if you want to get anywhere near an A or A+. It's not a bad class, you just can't procrastinate.

Easy class: DO THE PROJECTS THEY ARE WORTH ALOT OF YOUR GRADE. Literally, as long as you follow the instructions you will be good. Weekly discussions(online),3 quizzes. She grades everything at the end of the quarter so if that worries you maybe not. As long as you do well on most the content, im not sure its possible to get below a B in the class.

DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR BEGGS! Although she is very nice and her class is pretty easy she DOESNT grade anything until finals week. That is unprofessional and inconsiderate because this entire quarter I have had a 100% due to just doing the hw that is pre graded. There were 3 quizzes that she never graded and those quizzes could tank the grade.

The class is based on an online book about art, which was quite boring in my opinion. 1 assignment (done on the book website) and 1 discussion per week. Reading is required for the assignments but you don't need to read since answers can be found online. 1 midterm and 1 final (both similar to the assignments every week).

The lectures are interesting but can get a little boring at times. Each week you work with a group on an in class assignment and turn it in at the end. Makes you take a photo of your group to submit online for attendance. 1 MC exam online and 1 MC final in person. 1 group presentation. EC available if you go to a museum.

Class done on Canvas and M-H Connect. Weekly homework and discussion, midterm, final exam, and extra credit assignment. Weekly homework based on assigned chapter, can get pretty long, 50+ questions. Discussions require multiple replies, but pretty easy. Midterm and final pretty straightforward, take notes on lectures to study.

Class was async. We had readings and a set of multiple choice questions that we had to do every week or two. Those were graded on completion but they could take up to an hour to complete. We also had discussion posts.

One discussion post and a chapter reading assignment due each week. The ch reading assignment was graded based off of completion, but it wasn't difficult either. You have to reply to two students' discussion post. One midterm and one final that were pretty much the same format. Both were easy. Highly recommend this class if you want an easy "A."

Prof Nguyen includes a lot of class participation in his lectures, so make sure to pay attention bc he tends to call on random students. Hw was quite intensive as it could reach to over 30 pages of work, but the deadlines were sort of decent. He is also not flexible with due dates! and hw is weighed the most so make sure not to skip it :)

He was nice. I didn't vibe with the group-heavy format of the class and he wouldn't ever explain the answer when he was asked a question, just giving us examples without really explaining how he is getting from point A to point B.

awesome professor and teaches concepts very well. allows one sided cheat sheets for exams and double sided for the final. homework and in class material was not on the final, lots of multiple choice but it can be tricky. very caring professor and is lenient on grading but only if you participate in class, biased towards those who talk more.

I understand why people were intimidated by him as a teacher, but I really liked him, and I suck at math. He is reasonable as a person, and if you show up to class and engage with him we will like you more and probably be more lenient w grading. Teaches by calling people out a bit but he's not aggressive. Teaches concepts reallyyy well.

He was a good professor I just wasn't used to the flipped classroom approach. He gives out a decent amount of homework but gave us all 24 hours to do the quizzes, midterms, and the final exam making it pretty flexible. Most of what we did in class was review from the videos we had to watch but I still recommend going to get that extra practice in.
Shao Yang is very knowledgeable and his class contains useful information for interpretation subjects.
Professor Shao Yang is very knowledgeable about Chinese/English translation

This introductory course offers an excellent foundation in translation theory and practice. Professor Shao is always well-prepared, ensuring that every minute is used effectively. While the homework assignments are light, they are thoughtfully designed to help us apply what we learned to practical translation tasks. I highly recommend this class!

Professor Shao is an exceptional instructor who delivers engaging and informative classes. I have had the pleasure of taking both MAND51 and M AND054 with him and have consistently found his classes to be both stimulating and rewarding. If you are looking for a translation course, I wholeheartedly recommend Professor Shao's class.
Definitely lots of very helpful information if the students intend to improve their translation skills from English to Chinese.

Loved this Professor. Quick to respond in emails and the class was completely asynch. Tests were take home. Homework is graded by completeness but a few problems are chosen by random that are marked for corectness.
Good professor. Homework is graded partially by completion but he picks out a few problems for correctness. Exams aren't bad, they are "take-home"-style exams. Very straightforward class.

Homework is a staggering 30% of your grade, but all homework is graded quite strictly based on correctness and not completion. The lectures are quite long, but they do explain the course content well. Overall a good professor, just make sure to triple check your homework.
All you could ever really ask for in a professor. Incredibly caring, responsive, well-spoken, and reasonable. If you have the opportunity, take him, you won't regret it.

Kristin was an amazing professor she really cares about her students. She gives a lot of work each week, but it's really easy! the whole class is basically peer-review. She grades on if it's submitted or not. The only thing is our final is a portfolio that is given to the English board, and they determine if we pass the class or not.

I took her class in April 2024, and she is an excellent teacher. She supports every student, making the class enjoyable and the materials well-prepared. This is the best one I've ever attended compared to other writing classes. I highly recommend it.

I highly recommend Professor Agius as she is a very kind and caring professor. She was one of my very first English instructors who made me appreciate the English language and literature. She helped me in many ways to expand my mind and learn so much about myself. She is such a great feedback giver I took her for both EWRT 1 & 2.

There are reading and writing assignments due throughout each week. You get full credit for just completing them. She really wants students to learn and engages us in the classroom. She's a very good teacher! She's also very kind and understanding, checking in with students when she notices they're falling behind.
She is a pretty good teacher who tries to make the class as interactive as possible. As long as you do the online work that she provides consistently, this class is an easy A.

Great professor! Definitely one of the most interesting and engaging 2+ hr classes I've taken. Class regularly ended 30mins early and you spend most of the time split up into small groups. Her study guides are identical to the tests so if you pay attention during lectures and do the homework, it's an easy A. If you're on the fence, take this class!

Professor Ahrends makes class fun which is important for learning a new language. I had her for a year and she is an excellent teacher. She is very fair and makes every effort for students to be successful in her courses.

I took her German 3 class and she was one of the best professors I took at De Anza. She is really caring and the class has a real sense of community. But you do have to put the work in to succeed in her class.

I took her German 3 class and she was one of the best professor I took at De Anza. She is really caring and the class has a real sense of community. But you do have to put the work in to succeed in her class.

Knowledgeable professor who wants students to succeed. Helpful inside and outside the classroom. Participation is essential as is attendance. Not always hip to modern German youth culture and language as she has been in the US for many years. Unfortunately Dr Chiriaeva has ceded the German program to her in full due to low enrollment. Worth taking!
Although professional and detailed in his approach, Professor Lee is personable and fun. I'd highly recommend his courses.
Wish more profs would be like him. Treats students with respect and like they're adults (which we are lol).

Professor Lee teaches in the paralegal department at De Anza College. Course work was thorough and in-class discussions were helpful. The textbooks were not always clear, but lectures included a lot of content that the students could relate to. Good course.

Professor Lee is in the top 3 professors I've ever had and not just at De Anza or in community college, but in university as well. If you are interested in the law, take Lee. I've taken several classes with him and just wish there were more to take.

As a night school student Lee is stimulating and personable. He text choice was solid and I have used it in later courses. The expectations are very clear. He is a fan of the Socratic method so be sure to complete assigned reading or you will feel put on the spot. I would definitely take more classes with Lee.
For his class at Miramar. Major opportunities to get ahead of the class. Very clear expectations. Homework is light and can be completed in one to two sittings.

Professor Claros is exactly what you'd want out of a college professor. He seems like he genuinely cares and gives feedback on your assignments, even online. He's fair and doesn't throw unexpected stuff in your face, and genuinely wants to help you succeed. Would absolutely recommend taking a class with him if you're able.
Randy was pretty funny, I took him for Human sexuality and it was a pretty fun class. Do your homework and try to finish the essay's on time so you can get a better grade.

Professor Claros is a great professor and you can really tell he's involved and likes what he does. Class lectures are almost always interesting and he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. Tests are all open note and open book, there are 3 papers, and one group project. Overall, theres a lot of work but he makes it fun and interesting.

Easy A. Expect to attend class since the pop quizzes are based on lecture but the quizzes are open notes which makes it easy. The class itself is pretty funny and enjoyable. I would definitely take this class again. He's an awesome professor. You don't need a textbook but this class requires you to purchase an access code for the personality test.
Weisner's lectures can be long, but engaging if you participate. Though a gen ed, the writing assignments need effort. For study prep, Unstuck study and the textbook proved helpful.

Weisner has long in-class lectures and monologues that are mandatory, and if you miss more than two classes, then your grade is affected. Even though you would think that poetry would be an easy A since its only a general ed class, you definitely need to put some effort into the writing assignments he has since he is a harsh grader.

Though sometimes he may wildly misinterpret your poems Ken was an amazing teacher, made me regret not being an English major. I used the class as a way to practice writing poetry and it was really accessible no matter how you approach it. Expect to write a lot of replies tho.

I think because I particularly enjoy writing and english, this class was very fun for me. If you do all the work and the essays, you should do well in the class. Its not very hard. The quizzes were open note and were very easy, the discussions were super easy. Just participate and actually try and you get credit. On essays-show effort.
Not the most clear when it comes to asking for help and tough when grading essays

AN ABSOLUTE SWEET HEART. She's extremely caring, and gives great feedback. She provides feedback for every part of your writing, and is clear about what she expects, Fairly easy class, I definitely recommend her

She is a very nice and excellent professor. I will recommend her to every student who actually wants to learn college level essay writing. She will always grade you fairly and will always gives great feedbacks that will help you when you are writing an essay.
I loved having Professor Kurth as an English teacher. Although you do a lot of writing in this course, she gives you lots of time and great feedback. Highly recommend:)

I LOVE PROFESSOR KURTH. She's the best professor I've had here at DeAnza. She's super sweet and gives amazing feedback. I took her class online through zoom and she would stay after hours if you have any questions. I definitely recommend taking her.

Lita is super sweet and considerate but her grading is a little tough, you need to adapt to her grading style quick and if you're a good writer, you're set. some of her assignments are strange but honestly, overall easy class

Such a chill and free course. Literally just small quizzes each week and online discussion. Can be all completed all within a week or less if you put in the work. The final was just an essay--- not bad at all. He is very clear with his grading at the start of class. Super quick with email responses. Wish he didn't hide the grading section on canvas

Insanely easy class if you want to spend $180 for the textbook. I took his asynchronous class and didn't email him once or even receive a grade back during the entire quarter. Everything is participation and you have multiple attempts to get 100% on the tests and quizzes.
easiest class ever just pay for the textbook. tbh you could finish the whole course in 2 days
Good prof if u just care about getting an A and have $180 to spare.

Do yourself a favour and go get your "easy A" somewhere else.
You will not only learn nothing but the video lectures are so painfully boring!
This is the only class I have ever regretted. And will stay away from this teacher till eternity.
Kind, friendly and lovely professor! Truly cares about his students:) Would definitely recommend this professor!

Really easy online summer class, a couple group discussions + individual assignments every week, takes about 5-15 minutes per assignment to finish, a short easy quiz every week, gave free pdf's of textbooks, never had meetings with him but seemed nice whenever he replied to messages, definitely would take if your self-paced.

Stay away from this class if you think of taking it as an asynchronous one. You will get no feedback on any of your work (including the final essay) and no grade until the very last week of the class or so. Very disappointing experience, especially for a critical thinking class where you would expect more participation from the teacher.

In week 1 there is very little to do, 2 group discussions & 2 replies to other classmates for each discussion. I am writing this rating after seeing the workload of week 2. The required reading for week 2 is over 60 pages long altogether, 3 group discussions with multiple parts & 1-page analysis. This class is asynchronous but a LOT of work.

A solid pick. Textbooks are given for free. The best part is that he responds super quickly to his text messages, making questions and feedbacks very accessible. Helpful feedbacks are given. No extra credits though, and class participation is a must.

Genuinely such a nice teacher who really cares about her students and their success. She gives a lot of feedback and grades essays very quickly. You do have to read a good amount but all the work was manageable and she doesn't grade hard at all.
Manageable workload if you stay on top of the assignments. Helpful professor, but attendance is mandatory. unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for study prep.

Very clear rubric for essays (four in total) and gave pretty good feedback. She seems very caring but I would say her lectures are not the best. She relied a lot on the assigned reading (which was free,) and she also had the students give presentations on grammar. She cares a lot about grammar and sentence structure.

Paseno is an excellent instructor, making class discussions interesting and enhancing our writing skills through the exploration of various literary styles, analysis essays, quoting techniques, and bibliography presentations. You will not regret taking her class if you're serious about improving your writing abilities.

Julie is an incredible teacher who genuinely cares about her students. I had her for ELIT 46B and EWRT 1B. She holds you up to high standards and will rarely give out 100%s on essays, so show up, be present, and do your best. Slacking will not get you an A with her. Her lectures have stuck with me for years, and I wish I could take her again!

Out of my entire collegiate career, this was the instructor that, by far, had the clearest grading criteria. She communicates her expectations very exactly. Do the homework and keep up with the vocabulary and grammar, and you'll do well.

I do not get how she has such low ratings. I do watch anime regularly, but most of the Japanese I have learned is from this class. Lectures can be long but just pay attention, and you will do well. It just contains such simple concepts to the point I multitask while listening to her lectures (I did that with reading manga lmaooo).

I dont know why her rate is low.
This class is easy A and you dont even have to study.
Quizzes and exams are super easy so that I havent even studied more than 1 hour.
I havent learned Japanese or watched anime, I was taking this class just for Igetc.
This means that even though I wasnt interested in japanese, I got an A+
just focus on her lecture

I took her JAP1 and JAP2. She only provides sources from youtube, so you need to watch all the videos to learn Japanese. She does not teach, but only grades your hw. She is very strict, and proud of herself for her studies, amazing Narcissism. So you never try to argue her, she might give you less grade than you suppose to get.

Terrible professor. Lost my homework multiple times, gives unhelpful feedback and sent me passive-aggressive emails when I asked her questions about the lecture. If you already know Japanese and want an easy credit, then this is the class for you. If you don't, then be prepared. I worked my butt off and got an A+, but that was due to my own effort.

No tests/quizzes, each week was a lab handout worth 20 points, easy to get 100% if you answer all of the questions, extra credit was offered on the last class, very knowledgeable & funny, great teacher, willing to answer questions, overall a great and easy class

Very active and caring professor. She grades everything fairly and gives constructive feedback. Her exams are similar to her quizzes and are very straightforward. I would recommend definitely this professor.
Very low stress/manageable class with straightforward assignments. Would def recommend if you need a science class for credits. Professor is also very nice. Def would take again.
If you need the GE credits take this class. Super easy and useful

She is very understanding and accessible via email. There are weekly quizzes and sometimes discussions that can be completed fairly easily if the reading is done. The quizzes are open book which is very helpful.

His grading methodology is unorthodox, but as long as you put in the work to the standard he expects, it'll earn full points. Speech feedback is given via a rubric on Canvas, so be on the lookout for that in order to improve as the course progresses. It matters for the final speech. Make friends quickly: there's a group project assignment included.

Really good professor. Easy class. If u do he work, it'san easy A. In this class it's either you get a 0 or 100 for each assignment. Overall rly good. Encourages team work, had few quizzes and all were open book. 5 speeches and few powerpoints involved. Only effort needed is when giving a speech and writing evalutions. hella chill. 100% recommended

Just finished up the quarter and I really enjoyed his class. As long as you do the work, you will get an A. He gives a day to makeup speeches if you miss one! We take 3 tests and they are all the same and open book! You're also allowed to work on it with your table groups! Overall, he gave awesome lectures and I highly recommend his class.

Easy A course. I strongly recommend this course to international students. There are 4 tests, same question every time, all answer can be found in textbook, study guide is given. Speech outline and 5 live speech recordings will always100%, as long as you do the work. Watch lecture video and expect to write around 150-300 words every week.

Pretty straightforward (your speech will be assigned to a classmate to peer review and you'd do the same). As long as you do the work you're bound to get an A. His videos explaining each speech are actually really precise so you can just follow those. Plus he gives an outline for every speech. Tests answers are in the study guide!

This is a self-paced course where the professor's lectures aren't too helpful. Focus on the zyBooks, labs, and projects to learn the material. Unstuck study can be a great study aid alongside other resources like ChatGPT. Overall, an easy A if you're diligent.
Zoom meetings were optional and most of his zoom classes were just going over slides. As long as you pace yourself and learn the material through zybooks and the labs you should do perfectly fine.

The professor's lectures are just slow reading of PPTs, fortunately there is no attendance requirement and the weekly assignments are: zybooks, codelab and projects that take 8-12 hours per week.The professor's program requirements are vague. There were two exams, midterm and final, both less difficult than the usual assignments.

He is an experienced professor. Ask question, and he will try his best to answer. The only negative side was that the lectures were centered around the student asking rather than professor teaching. He cares about the style of your code, so be careful.

Also, he does not teach the theories behind the codes, so you need to do that on your own.

EZZ AF FREE A+ 
self study class, hes a nice guy but you won't learn much from him. just go to zoom and mute the audio after he takes attendance. make sure you listen in on the day before exams though, he gives hints and tells you what topic each question will be on. its literally impossible to get lower than an A unless ur a smooth brained monkey

Once a week discussions on Canvas that are graded on participation. Three papers ranging from 1-6 pages minimum throughout the course. Lectures almost entirely through the whole class, with usually one discussion in between. An easy class, but if you can't stand to listen to long lectures once a week, I wouldn't take him.

Took him for a GE and he's honestly great professor! Extremely passionate about the topics and gave engaging lectures. Class consisted of lecture and then group discussion. Assignments were simple and papers were easy as long as you put in effort. His lectures just explained the "required" readings, but I found his explanations to be better.

Intense amount of readings and music to analyze. Prerecorded lectures have uneven audio quality, but you really need them to understand readings. Was ready to drop class until listening to one. Weekly discussions with 200-300 words, three papers ranging from 1-7 pages. Gives very detailed, helpful feedback on papers, which is rare

Heavy Reading and the class consisted of weekly discussion on canvas and 3 papers including a final that was 3k words. He has a very deep passion for what he teaches but I just found it rather boring and uninteresting.

Gives good constructive feedback to improve on your papers. Would have given a 5 but the subject is not really my interest, so I find the discussions a little boring. Tons of reading each week, but if you are falling behind on those, make sure to attend his lectures as he explains each topic in depth. Easy A if you finish your work on time.
Great choice to choose Arts History to learn from this professor. Through the in-person reviews of each lecture, I was able to gain insight on the importance of understanding art.

Ridiculously easy class. Assignments are a breeze and take very little time to complete. The course content isn't the most interesting, but I would still recommend this class for an easy way to complete a GE requirement.

I took the trouble to spend 30-40 minutes each assignment to make sure that my grade would maintain an A, but every single assignment I would receive a below passing grade and whenever I would ask her via email/canvas comments on what I could do to improve, I would get a cold one line text that didn't even apply to what I was asking.

Professor Joplin's class is straightforward if you stay on top of the reading and discussions. unstuckstudy proved helpful for prep, alongside the course materials. Though communication could be improved, it's generally an easy A-level GE credit.

Very easy assignments, does have high word count requirements (sometimes 500 words minimun) but you can type word vomit and have it done in 30 min if you cared a lot about it. She is mostly nice but does not respond to emails, it's a gamble, sometimes it'll take a day for her to respond sometimes a week (very annoying if you need your stuff graded)

I had an okay experience in her class but wouldn't prefer to take her again. I emailed her once with a few questions and she took almost a week to respond. Assignments were pretty easy and her feedback was always really kind, but I personally didn't find the assignments to be too helpful/worthwhile.

Professor Wann was a good professor but beware for a lot of assignments. However, the assignments often helped with the essays. There were 4 essays and she allowed extensions on all of them, overall super caring and kind!

Prof Wann grades things easily except for essays. 1 discussion a week that can use in essays. 4 essays which gets harder. 1 chapter+activity a week & 1 book to read in 4 weeks for last essay. Not recommend if you're taking a lot of classes. I'm not good at writing, 2 last essays took me around 7-8hrs to finish. Her instruction is unclear sometimes.

4 essays, graded kinda fairly, doesn't really respond to comments about grading.
